title: Army officers visiting the Utah ranch followed home by phenomena

tellings.quote: people have described people who were you know trained army officers who went to the ranch a few days went home and boom they there was some phenomenon following them

experienced more of is the Skinwalker Ranch stuff where people come come out of you know exper being at Skinwalker Ranch studying stuff there and they say stuff follows me around in my home and I have to rid myself of it
tellings.difference: Told by the host about researchers studying at the ranch in general, not trained army officers, and adds that they have to rid themselves of it.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the Utah ranch lore that people who visit Skinwalker Ranch are followed home by phenomena.

as_told.title: Skinwalker Ranch phenomena follow people home

tellings.quote: Um if you look at the testimony of Jake Barber or even look at the people under Bigalow, you know, studying, you know, stuff at Skinwalker Ranch, these things seem to sort of follow them home.
tellings.difference: Names Jake Barber and the people working under Bigelow as the ones followed home, where the story speaks of army officers.
tellings.link_reason: Both say people who studied things at Skinwalker Ranch were followed home by phenomena. Michels' own telling in that story says almost the same thing.

as_told.title: Jake Barber and Skinwalker Ranch researchers followed home by phenomena

tellings.quote: in skinwalkers at the pentagon colm kelleher george knapp and james lakatsky report hitchhiker effects among many of the scientists that studied at skinwalker ranch in fact the phenomenon often followed these people home
tellings.difference: Credits the claim to the book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon by Kelleher, Knapp and Lacatski, and names it the 'hitchhiker effect'.
tellings.link_reason: Both make the same general claim that people who studied at Skinwalker Ranch under Bigelow were followed home by the phenomenon. The story's Jesse Michels tellings say this about the Bigelow researchers.

plain: People who spent time at a ranch in Utah studying strange events there say the strangeness followed them home. The veteran UFO researcher Jacques Vallée tells Michels he has heard of 'trained army officers who went to the ranch a few days, went home and boom' found 'some phenomenon following them.' Michels returns to it on several episodes and calls the place Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for reports of odd lights, creatures and other events. He says researchers there report that 'stuff follows me around in my home and I have to rid myself of it.' He names the people who studied the ranch for the businessman Robert Bigelow, and a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he retrieved a UFO, as people things seemed to follow. In one episode Michels credits the claim to the book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon by Colm Kelleher, George Knapp and James Lacatski, which he says reports a 'hitchhiker effect' among many scientists who worked at the ranch. Vallée tells it as reports passed to him, and Michels as something he has read and heard. Vallée speaks of army officers, while Michels speaks of scientists and researchers. If true, it would mean whatever is at the ranch is not tied to the place but can attach itself to people.
